title: Reflection Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of reflection fundamentals using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates reflection fundamentals.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Reflection Fundamentals** as part of **Annotations, Reflection, and Code Generation**. Annotations and code-generation tools add metadata or generated code; reflection has runtime/tooling costs and Kotlin reflection/JVM APIs have their own maturity considerations. Use the subtopics—Runtime Introspection, Inspecting Classes and Properties, Callable References and Reflection—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Annotations and code-generation tools add metadata or generated code; reflection has runtime/tooling costs and Kotlin reflection/JVM APIs have their own maturity considerations.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with runtime introspection. Then compare it with inspecting classes and properties. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Runtime Introspection
items.text: Runtime Introspection means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Inspecting Classes and Properties
items.text: Inspecting Classes and Properties should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Callable References and Reflection
items.text: Callable References and Reflection is one part of reflection fundamentals. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Reflection examples may require kotlin-reflect; processor/compiler-plugin examples require an isolated Gradle project and compatible tooling.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Reflection is always faster and safer than a direct API.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
